author: fester
body: Stage 3. Re-derives the two claims that reached this wire only in C2.3a: no call escapes the effect row its caller declares, and every linear parameter is used exactly once on every path.

author: fester
body: Before that change neither claim was checkable from IR text at all. A `linear T` and a `T` produced byte-identical output, and an arrow's effect row was bound and discarded, so a function lost its effects the moment it took a parameter. Both facts were enforced by the front end and thrown away at the boundary. That is why this stage is last: the input did not exist.

author: fester
body: Effects reach a signature by two routes and both have to be read, or the check reports against a declaration it failed to see. A nullary definition's effects ride in EffectfulTy, because its type is not an arrow and has no row to carry them. A multi-parameter function is curried, so its row sits on an inner arrow and the outer one is empty: reading only the outermost row would find nothing declared on exactly the functions that declare the most.

author: fester
body: An effect is covered when the caller declares it by name, or declares the family a dotted operation belongs to: a body performing `Console.Write` is within a signature that declares `Console`, which is how the effect declarations in this tree are written.

author: fester
body: A linear parameter must be mentioned exactly once. Counting mentions is the whole of it at this stage: a name used twice is a double use and a name never used is a leak, and both are refused by the front end (CDX2061 and CDX2063), so either one appearing here is a disagreement.

author: fester
body: The two arms of a conditional are alternatives, not a sequence: a value consumed once in each branch is consumed once on every path. Adding them would report every correct use in an if as a double use.

author: fester
body: A chapter grounds the hardware effects it is the SOURCE of, and its bodies may then perform exactly those without declaring them. The table rides the wire as "slug\neffect" entries and a def's entries are the ones whose slug half equals its own chapter-slug. Because a slug can hold no newline, comparing up to the separator is an exact slug match and never a prefix collision with a longer slug.

author: fester
body: The grounded names JOIN the declared set rather than short-circuiting the check, which is the whole of why this is not an exemption: a chapter that grounds Device.Port and performs Device.Mmio is still reported, and the dotted family rule in rc-eff-covered applies to a grounded name exactly as it does to a declared one.

author: fester
body: Until 2026-08-04 this table was not on the wire at all and could not be consulted. It cost 90 of the 97 findings of the first complete sweep, every one of them a chapter carrying a grounds clause, and the test for the grounds feature itself was among them.

author: fester
body: A callee whose own type carries effect labels is performing them, so the caller must declare them. This is the boundary the README sentence claims cannot be crossed undeclared.
